messages:
Amanda L.: Heads up — we have a customer-reported latency regression (p95/p99) for inference routes in eu-west-1 since last deploy. Dashboards show p95 ~420ms -> 1.6s, p99 hitting 3.4s. Cache miss ratio for prefix KV up ~6x. Can someone triage?
Raj P.: On it. Which model/route? any customer IDs?
Amanda L.: Route: /v1/generate (gpt-medium-quant). A few customers (acct 3245) saw errors but mostly high tail latency. I linked the dashboard: https://dash.company/reports/latency?region=eu-west-1&route=generate
Liam T.: I'm seeing a spike in prefix-cache evictions around 02:15 UTC. eviction rate spiked and cold-starts increased. Suspect fragmentation + lots of unique header keys.
Sofia M.: Logs show header normalization changed in that deploy (PR #5481) — inbound trace-id X-Request-Id header now included in cache key unintentionally.
Ben C.: oh no. That would blow up cardinality. Can you grep example?
Sofia M.: snippet from runtime logs: "prefix_key=route:/v1/generate|hdr:trace-id=abc123|user-agent=OpenAI-Client" — trace-id should be filtered out.
Raj P.: Repro quick check: running a high qps synthetic with randomized trace ids -> cache hit rate drops from 92% to 18% and p95 jumps. Command I ran: 
```
wrk -t4 -c200 -d60s http://eu-west-1-infer.internal/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer x' -H 'X-Trace-Id: rand'
```

Liam T.: Good repro. Root cause: header canonicalization missed the blacklist for X-Trace-Id. Also eviction policy (LRU with small TTL) + shard imbalance causes jitter.
Amanda L.: Immediate mitigation? Can we patch the key builder to ignore trace headers and roll a canary?
Ben C.: I pushed a hotfix to runtime to canonicalize headers and drop X-Trace-Id from keying. Canary deployed to eu-west-1 canary pool (ops-bot started rollout).
ops-bot: Canary rollout started for runtime-hotfix-5481 to node-pool eu-west-1-canary (30% traffic). Monitoring p95/p99.
Sofia M.: Meanwhile, suggest raising prefix TTL from 30s -> 300s for affected routes to reduce churn while we validate. That avoids repeated warmups.
Raj P.: I've applied temporary TTL override in config for /v1/generate in eu-west-1. Observing metrics: cache hit went 18% -> 62% within 90s, p95 dropping toward baseline.
Liam T.: Also enabling sticky-prefix pinning for heavy customers to avoid shard spillover. Will schedule a follow-up to evaluate long-term eviction policy (LFU vs LRU) and shard rebalancing.
Ben C.: Canary looks good for 10m — no regressions and key normalization fixed. ops-bot: proceed with full rollout?
ops-bot: Full rollout initiated to eu-west-1, 100% in 6 minutes.
Amanda L.: Great. Please create postmortem with timeline, root cause (header canonicalization bug + small TTL + shard imbalance), and mitigations: revertable hotfix, TTL emergency knob, header-blacklist tests. Assign owners.
Raj P.: I'll own the postmortem + test to assert header-blacklist in unit tests. Liam will own eviction policy follow-up. Sofia will add E2E with randomized headers to detect regressions.
Ben C.: Also add a runtime lint to fail PRs that add header-to-key mappings without a reviewer tag.
Amanda L.: Thanks team. I'll update support ticket and let customer know we mitigated and are doing follow-ups.
Raj P.: FYI I archived the repro script and query: 
metrics query: SELECT time, p95_latency, prefix_cache_hit_rate FROM route_metrics WHERE route='/v1/generate' AND region='eu-west-1' AND time > now() - interval '2 hours';
repro: https://git.company/repro-scripts/kv-cardinality-spike.sh
Amanda L.: Closing thread; follow-ups tracked in PM-3456. :white_check_mark:
